metadata.concept_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.objective: Explore how health-conscious adults 18-35 navigate sugar-free carbonated beverage choices — from concrete product attributes (zero-sugar sweetener identity, caffeine dose, carbonation intensity, can design, price per 12-pack, availability at their usual grocery) to the functional consequences they produce (no 2pm crash, alertness without jitters, satisfying the soda craving without calories) to the psychosocial consequences they enable (feeling in control, belonging at a rooftop bar without a cocktail, signaling a modern wellness identity without preaching) to the deeper values these consequences serve (autonomy over ingredient choices, vitality, authenticity in lifestyle signaling, belonging with peers who are cutting back on alcohol, pragmatism over purity). Treat category alternatives — Coke Zero, LaCroix, Celsius — as contrast references when respondents describe why a given attribute led them to choose or reject a product.

turns.question: So I'm really curious about the drinks you actually reach for day-to-day—the ones without sugar, like the zero-sugar sodas or sparkling drinks. Can you walk me through a time recently when you grabbed one of those instead of something else? What was going on, and what made you pick that particular drink in that moment?
turns.response: I guess the main thing is I'll grab a zero-sugar soda if I'm already thinking about cutting back, or like, if I've had a bunch of regular stuff that week. There's not really a specific moment—it's more just kind of automatic at the store sometimes. I'll see it and think "yeah, might as well" instead of the regular version. Honestly don't feel super strongly about it either way though.

turns.question: When you're at the store and that automatic reach happens, what else about ZeroFizz or similar drinks makes that grab feel easy?
turns.response: Honestly the taste is probably the biggest thing. I know diet drinks can taste kinda off, but ZeroFizz doesn't have that weird aftertaste I get with other ones. And then it's just... the can design is pretty clean, so it doesn't feel like you're grabbing something unhealthy even though it's sugar-free.
